speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. I see you're experiencing agitation and yellowing of the skin and eyes, which suggests jaundice. To help narrow down the cause, can you tell me if you have had any abdominal pain, fever, or changes in the color of your urine or stools?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. Do you have any nausea, vomiting, or abdominal pain, and have you noticed any dark urine or pale stools?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The lab results show severe liver dysfunction with elevated enzymes and bilirubin, but the normal hepatitis serology rules out common viral causes like Hepatitis A, B, or C. Given your history of drug use, particularly ecstasy and cocaine, this presentation is highly suggestive of acute liver failure due to a toxic agent or metabolic complication.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal acetaminophen level and urine toxicology screen rule out common drug overdoses, yet the severely reduced prothrombin activity and high bilirubin indicate acute liver failure. Given your history of high-risk sexual behavior and drug use, we must consider other viral causes like Hepatitis E or autoimmune hepatitis, as well as vascular issues.

speaker: Doctor
text: With viral, autoimmune, and common toxic causes ruled out, and given your history of ecstasy and cocaine use, I suspect a toxic injury from a contaminant like Poppers (amyl nitrite) or a rare reaction to the drugs themselves. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute liver failure due to recreational drug toxicity (likely nitrite inhalant or adulterant)
